content.title: Didi posts Q2 loss of $350 million on lawsuit provision, despite revenue growth
content.summary: Chinese ride-hailing giant Didi Global reported on Thursday a second-quarter net loss of 2.5 billion yuan ($350 million), driven by a one-off charge, even as revenue rose 10.9%, partly fuelled by growth in overseas business. The loss was largely due to a provision of 5.3 billion yuan for a previously disclosed shareholder lawsuit, while spending on marketing and other expense also increased, reflecting intensifying domestic competition. Didi maintains its dominant position in China's ride-hailing sector, but pressure from rivals is mounting.

content.title: Chinese firms in legal battle over Brazil food delivery
content.summary: SAO PAULO (Reuters) -A Brazilian subsidiary of China's ride-hailing company DiDi Global sued Chinese rival Keeta on Monday in a Sao Paulo court alleging trademark infringement and unfair competition, according to court documents seen by Reuters.  The lawsuit comes days after Keeta, which is entering the Brazilian market, sued DiDi's Brazilian unit, 99, in Brazil, alleging its food delivery app 99Food was trying to restrict restaurants from working with more than two delivery platforms.  In Monday's lawsuit, 99 accused Keeta, owned by Chinese delivery giant Meituan, of using colors, graphics and font similar to 99's platform to "catapult its commercial operations" in the Brazilian market.
